headlines.title: 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio, pleads no contest to charges
headlines.description: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio, according to the Columbiana County Jail. Jail officials said York was originally arrested on suspicion of solicitation of prostitution and possessing criminal tools. The criminal tool in question was a cellphone, according to officials. York posted bail and was released Sunday. On Monday morning, York pleaded no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

headlines.title: 1 dead after fiery crash on I-580 in Livermore
headlines.description: A fatality was reported after a crash early Monday morning on Interstate Highway 580 in Livermore, according to the California Highway Patrol. Around 3:30 a.m., the CHP said it closed westbound I-580 near the southbound Livermore Avenue exit due to the crash. The lanes reopened around 5:15 a.m. There were no further details about the fatality immediately released.

headlines.title: Vegetation fire makes its way into solar facility in Sonoma County
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a vegetation fire near Highway 101 in the North Bay that Cal Fire said made its way into a solar facility Sunday. According to Cal Fire, the vegetation fire was reported near Highway 101 and San Antonio Road in Sonoma County. The fire, dubbed the Petaluma Fire, has grown to four acres and made its way into a solar facility. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Carquinez Bridge, stretch of Highway 101 reopen after weekend closures
headlines.description: The Carquinez Bridge and a busy stretch of Highway 101 in San Francisco are fully open for the Monday morning commute after Caltrans completed two major weekend projects ahead of schedule. The westbound Interstate 80 span of the Carquinez Bridge, which carries traffic southbound toward the Bay Area, reopened at midnight after being closed since Friday night. Crews installed a new layer of asphalt on the bridge during the closure. Caltrans said it had been 23 years since the span received this type of work and officials hope the new pavement will last another 20 years. Caltrans also completed work early on Highway 101 near Hospital Curve in San Francisco, with all lanes reopening around 1 a.m. Monday. The highway had been reduced to two lanes in each direction over the weekend while crews performed what Caltrans described as crucial drainage improvements. The work is intended to make the section of Highway 101 less prone to flooding.

headlines.title: Bay Area fire crews help fight Hawk Fire in Nevada
headlines.description: Bay Area fire crews were deployed overnight to help fight the Hawk Fire near Reno, which has spread to more than 15,000 acres. The Hawk Fire started late Saturday and grew, quickly driven by strong winds. As of Sunday evening, the blaze left six people hurt, more than 5,000 others without power and thousands affected by the evacuation orders. As 800 firefighters battle the flames, thousands are leaving or ready to go. “Currently, we have 42,000 individuals who are displaced and on an active evacuation with approximately 45,000 individuals that are in the status to be prepared to evacuate,” U.S. Forest Service Incident Commander Shane Ackerson. Authorities confirmed the fire was human-caused, but haven’t said if it was suspected as arson. Local fire agencies were mobilized by Cal OES to help on the fire lines. Overnight, a group left Oakland, two engines from different Bay Area departments and one engine and battalion chief from Oakland and San Francisco, as well. “San Francisco was called early this morning a little bit after 1 a.m. to help with fires in the Reno area, we sent two type six fire engines which are larger pickup trucks style fire engines which are more maneuverable than most of the larger fire engines that people are familiar with,” San Francisco Fire Department Capt. Mariano Elias said. The state agreement allows for fast aid while maintaining protection for California. Closer to the fire, people are trying to stay safe, watching and waiting for word. Annemarie Anaya, who used to live in the Bay Area but moved to the Reno area just over a year ago, was one of the residents who had to evacuate. “I packed what I could and we loaded both cars, like I said electricity went off so my husband had to at least get the garage open to get the car out the garage and we just headed away,” she said. “It happened so fast, the winds kicked up and it just took over, so I know that the firefighters and the officials everyone is doing what they can I just hope everyone stays safe.”

headlines.title: Young man dies after being shot in a shopping center parking lot in El Cerrito
headlines.description: A young man died after being shot in the parking lot of a shopping center in El Cerrito Sunday, according to the police department. Police said they received a call of a shooting in the parking lot of the Del Norte Plaza Shopping center, located at 11299 San Pablo Avenue, at around 12:17 p.m. There, authorities said they found a young man who had been shot in the parking lot near Los Moles Restaurant. The man died at the scene, according to police. Officials said witnesses reported the suspects were in an altercation with the victim at his car and shot him. After the shooting, police said the suspects drove away southbound on S. 56th Street in a dark colored sedan. According to police, the witnesses said one of the suspects was wearing a black mask and a black North Face brand puffy jacket. The other suspect, police said, was wearing a hat and a black Nike brand jacket. The police department asks anyone with information to contact them at 510-237-3233.

headlines.title: Abandoned railway trestle near EBMUD plant in Oakland catches fire
headlines.description: An abandoned railway trestle near the East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD) caught fire Saturday night in Oakland, according to firefighters. Just after 10 p.m. on Saturday, Oakland Fire said crews were battling a fire on the old train trestles near the EBMUD plant. They had asked residents living 3 miles west of the intersection of West Grand Avenue and Wake Avenue to keep their windows and doors closed until air quality conditions could improve. Although firefighters were able to keep the fire from spreading to the building, they had to battle spot fires in the yard at the treatment plant. On Sunday, fire crews said they were cooling hot spots on the trestles and then will get heavy equipment to pull down the still smoldering infrastructure.

headlines.title: License plate reader network helps police locate missing Petaluma man 150 miles away
headlines.description: An at-risk missing adult was safely located more than 150 miles from his home after the Petaluma Police Department utilized an automated license plate reader network to track his vehicle across multiple counties. At approximately 6:38 p.m. on Aug. 21, Petaluma police received a report that a man with memory issues had left his residence earlier in the afternoon and had not returned, according to the department. Officers immediately entered him into the Missing and Unidentified Persons System (MUPS) as an at-risk missing adult and distributed his vehicle’s information to allied law enforcement agencies. During the investigation, police used the Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) network to search for the vehicle. An initial detection showed the man had traveled outside of Petaluma and into Solano County. As the evening progressed, additional Flock detections captured the vehicle continuing north through Lake and Mendocino counties. Each detection provided updated location and directional data, allowing Petaluma dispatchers to alert law enforcement agencies farther north. This coordination helped responding agencies focus their resources along the man’s anticipated route. When the system indicated the vehicle was heading toward Humboldt County, Petaluma police notified the Humboldt County Sheriff’s Office and the California Highway Patrol. At approximately 11:35 p.m., Humboldt County sheriff’s deputies safely located the man and his vehicle. His family was notified so arrangements could be made for his safe return. Petaluma police noted that the incident highlights the value of ALPR technology as an investigative tool during time-sensitive public safety incidents, allowing multiple jurisdictions to connect and focus their search efforts.

headlines.title: Pacific Grove Museum of Natural History names Samantha Weiss as new development director
headlines.description: The Pacific Grove Museum of Natural History has named Samantha “Sammi” Weiss as its new director of development and engagement, following the retirement of longtime director Susan Wolfe, museum officials announced Sunday. Weiss brings a background in scientific research, conservation, and philanthropy to the position. She holds a bachelor’s degree in animal sciences from Purdue University and a master’s degree in biology from Georgia Southern University. Before moving into nonprofit development, Weiss spent nearly a decade researching marine life, including the conservation and physiology of great white sharks. She now works to build philanthropic partnerships supporting education, conservation, and scientific research, the museum said. Weiss also serves in leadership roles with several Monterey County nonprofit organizations, including the Junior League of Monterey County, and the Monterey Bay Chapter of the Association of Fundraising Professionals. Museum Executive Director Rachel Miller said Wolfe made significant contributions during her tenure and welcomed Weiss as the museum prepares for its next phase of growth. Weiss will help lead the museum’s marketing strategy, reaccreditation efforts, strategic planning and fundraising initiatives, including efforts to strengthen community and donor relationships.

headlines.title: San Francisco retail landscape shifts as Union Square, Stonestown see renewed life
headlines.description: Shopping has long been a pastime for visitors and locals alike in San Francisco, but the city’s post-pandemic retail landscape is actively shifting. While some shopping districts have emptied out, others are expanding and bringing in new life. In Union Square, international fashion brand A Bathing Ape celebrated its grand opening with a block party featuring DJs and games. The opening marks a bright spot for an area that took a hit during the COVID-19 pandemic and the years following, suffering from declining foot traffic, rising crime, and the loss of major retailers like Saks Fifth Avenue. “It was awesome, that place is so cool, it’s so clean in there, and everything is just so aesthetic,” said Dustin Thurber of Sonoma County. More streetwear and experiential stores have been cropping up in Union Square to fill the void. Last year, Nintendo opened its first West Coast location in the district, and the San Francisco Chronicle reports that fashion brand Kith is working to take over the former Macy’s Men’s store. “It’s part of the revitalization of Union Square, bringing back some of the high-end retail to the area. It’s really, really important to us,” said Inder Bhatia, head of retail for A Bathing Ape. “We’ve had huge community support once we’ve opened up and it’s been really amazing thus far.” Just blocks away on Market Street, however, it is a different story. The once-busy San Francisco Centre remains boarded up. The nine-story building closed in January, and a deal to buy the mall fell through this summer. Meanwhile, on the western end of the city, Stonestown Galleria continues to draw consistent crowds with ample free parking and an expansive layout. The mall recently extended its hours, opening an hour earlier at 10 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays. “Downtown has been so dead since COVID, but Stonestown’s been pretty lively for the past few years. It’s rebounded pretty well from COVID in my experience,” said San Francisco resident Sam Dunn. Shoppers seem to be on board with the subtle changes and growing retail footprints in the area. “You got a lot of options, food court is amazing,” said Christian Bautista of San Francisco. “Probably, with the bringing of Raising Cane’s it’s gonna bring a lot of people together, you got a lot of options for clothing stores.” The success of these retail hubs has some shoppers hoping that more stores across the city will start staying open later to accommodate busy work schedules.

headlines.title: Elderly San Jose couple robbed of treasured heirloom in coordinated parking lot theft
headlines.description: A Sunday errand run turned into a nightmare for an elderly San Jose couple who lost a treasured heirloom in a highly coordinated robbery. The incident occurred last Sunday afternoon in the Almaden Plaza parking lot outside Costco. As the couple was finishing their grocery run and popped their trunk, two women immediately approached and began loading the groceries into their car. The 86-year-old husband told the women in Spanish, “It’s OK, I can by myself. I don’t need help, thanks.” The women persisted, replying, “God says we have to help the elderly.” The encounter quickly became unsettling. The 75-year-old wife said one of the women started kissing her hand and even handed her $20. Scared by the aggressive interaction, the wife threw the money to the ground. “They were quick to speak about religion and said, ‘You remind me of my mom that just passed away,'” the victims’ daughter said. According to the couple, one of the women followed the husband as he got into his car and offered to give him a necklace. “They are putting on this gift around Dad’s neck, and as they do, they are somehow removing his chain,” their daughter said. The women managed to steal the husband’s 18-karat gold medallion, an heirloom given to him by the priest who married the couple more than 50 years ago. He was left holding a fake chain in its place. The ordeal did not end there. The couple reported that a second car, containing at least two men, pulled up behind them and temporarily blocked their vehicle from leaving the parking lot. Nearly a week later, the couple remains in shock. They reported the robbery to the San Jose Police Department and stated they have become skeptical of people offering help and will no longer accept the kindness of strangers. Shoppers at Almaden Plaza expressed concern over the brazen theft. “I think people need to be more aware of their surroundings and be less trusting, especially if they flatter you,” said Richard, a San Jose shopper. San Jose police have not yet responded to inquiries regarding whether any arrests have been made or if similar robberies have been reported in the area.

headlines.title: Woman dies after suspected Richmond arson, bringing death toll to 4
headlines.description: The 33-year-old woman who was critically injured in a house fire allegedly set by her brother on Tuesday has died, the police department said on Saturday. Police said Sergio Rivera-Vega was accused of starting the fire at a home located along the 200 block of 15th Street on Tuesday night. The blaze killed Rivera-Vega’s 47-year-old father and his 5-year-old nephew, his 2-year-old niece and now his 33-year-old sister. Rivera-Vega lived in the home. Police said a motive for the alleged arson is still under investigation. “Our investigators, their number one goal is to figure out why this happened, why this person would do this to their family,” England said. “That is what everybody wants to know.” Richmond Aug 20 Richmond Aug 19 The day of the incident, firefighters had responded to a fire nearby at about 8:15 p.m. After that fire was under control at about 8:45 p.m., bystanders alerted them of another fire at a nearby home, which is the one Rivera-Vega allegedly started, according to authorities. The second fire was under control by about 9:25 p.m., according to officials. Three of the victims were taken to the hospital, where they died. The suspect’s father died at the scene. Police said all of the victims were injured or killed by the fire, and there is no evidence that they were shot or stabbed before the alleged arson.
